quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and let trains pass.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that railroad tracks are ahead. Slow down when you approach a railroad crossing. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop to let you turn.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.question: When changing lanes you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to signal your intentions.
Check for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be moving into your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: May be safely held by a strong adult.
Will be safe if they are standing on the floor in the back of the vehicle.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never be allowed to ride while standing in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use special child seats for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always secure children properly in a seat.

questions.question: When you want to make a right turn, your car must be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you begin to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road before making a right turn. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: If you need to drive in foggy weather:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive at a speed above 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when visibility is very poor. High beams reflect off fog and rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This green arrow on a lane use control signal means:

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means you can use that lane.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow rules that would be in place if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always obey a crossing guard's directions in a school zone. Slow down and be extra careful around children.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic flowing at a safe pace.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, you must yield. Wait for that vehicle to pass, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange.
Red.
Green.
Brown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown.
questions.explanation: Brown signs mark cultural, historical, and recreation areas. They are useful when you are traveling to places you do not know.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They warn that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different roads at the same time, which one must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, whether controlled by signs, signals, or not controlled, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right when both arrive at the same time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads divided by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the wheel tightly and stay in your lane. Slow down by taking your foot off the gas. When you are going very slowly, brake lightly and pull off the road to a safe spot.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait to proceed.
Honk before passing on the left.
Continue when you think children have finished getting off.
Pass before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus uses its stop signal. Do not move until the stop arm is put away.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell you what you must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell you what you must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular and white with black text. They tell drivers what rules to follow in an area, such as speed limits, no passing, or no turning.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road, what must you do?

options.text: Do not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane meant for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane meant for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must cross into the oncoming lane to pass. Only do this if it is safe and legal to pass.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Put your car in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, drive to the next intersection where you can turn safely from the proper lane.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Very dangerous.
Nothing to worry about.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Keeping your attention on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give a motorcycle a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, a motorcycle needs space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, or any emergency vehicle using a siren or air horn and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any instructions given by the emergency vehicle's loudspeaker. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so move only when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block the normal flow of traffic. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: This sign shows one type of:

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.
Lane change.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is coming. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles using a siren, air horn, and/or flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sit in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Sound your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, signal before carefully leaving the road. Turn on your hazard flashers. Park as far off the road as possible where other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to show that your vehicle is disabled.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake immediately.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake right away. Gradually slow down, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not move until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows down your reactions.
Makes you feel less confident.
Begins to break down more quickly.
Decreases the number of driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down your reactions.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more errors.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Follow what surrounding traffic is doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if the area were not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and use caution when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not following these directions is illegal and dangerous for construction workers.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while you are driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks while driving, keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift into neutral and press the brake steadily. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on their headlights.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, reduce your speed so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people crossing the street. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: May be moving or stationary.
Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down and pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones have orange signs with black lettering or symbols. Slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: You are driving when your power steering stops working. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with extra effort, reduce your speed, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with extra effort, reduce your speed, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you will need more effort to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to get around them.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give plenty of space. Bicyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too quickly or too close can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in the car because you are most likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car because you are most likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you stay in your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be unsafe.
